name: Qing dynasty

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 13.1 million km2 for the Early Qing (1644-1796). High = the ~14.7 million km2 peak usually quoted for c. 1790; low allows for loosely held Tibet and Mongolia. The world_1715 union (Manchu Empire + Tibet, protectorate from 1720) lacks Dzungaria and the Tarim basin, conquered 1755-59, which sit in the "central Asian khanates" polygon.

population.note: OWID/HYDE China 1750 = 178M, 1800 = 330M; the Qing dynasty article gives ~150M in 1700 doubling to ~300M by 1800 (Myers and Wang). 1760 interpolated; the 1762 baojia registration of ~200M (Ho Ping-ti) is the usual anchor.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Large absolute urban population but a falling urban share as rural population boomed; Beijing ~0.7-0.8M (Seshat 668,200-822,600 for 1700).

activePersonnel.note: Mid-18th century: over 200,000 bannermen and 600,067 Green Standard troops (Military of the Qing dynasty article; Elliott 2001 for the banners). Green Standard figure includes the provincial water forces.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Banner supernumeraries, Inner and Outer Mongol jasagh levies (19,500 Inner and 6,500 Outer Mongols served in the 1755 Ili campaign, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_Great_Campaigns), tusi native troops of the southwest.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Water-force crews of the Green Standard, gunners, commissariat and post-station personnel inside the 800,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Hereditary banner population (~2 million people in 1644, Elliott via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight_Banners, larger by 1760) plus Green Standard recruitment and Mongol levies; total war never tested.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Manchu and Mongol banner cavalry of the capital and provincial garrisons, the mounted core of the 200,000 bannermen (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Qing_dynasty).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: bow, lance, matchlock; armour largely ceremonial by 1760.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Qianlong revived the Mulan hunts as training amid declining banner discipline (Elliott 2001 pp. 184-186, 283-300 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Qing_dynasty).

count.note: Educated guess. Green Standard horse and Solon, Chahar and Mongol banner light cavalry used in the Dzungar campaigns.
Educated guess. Green Standard combat troops (zhanbing) with matchlocks and Han banner musketeers.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: Qianlong called incompetence with firearms a "common and pervasive disease" of the Green Standard (Waley-Cohen 2006 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_the_Qing_dynasty).

count.note: Educated guess. Green Standard garrison and police troops (shoubing) dispersed in small posts.
Educated guess. Kangxi took 235 cannon with 32,000 men in 1696 (~7 per 1,000 men, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dzungar%E2%80%93Qing_Wars); garrison guns mostly static.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: Jesuit-designed cast pieces of the 1670s, little later development.

count.note: Educated guess. Large war junks of the Fujian, Zhejiang and Guangdong water forces; the article calls the Qing navy the largest in East Asia but poorly organised.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: junks with few guns, far behind European line ships.

count.note: Educated guess. Patrol boats and river craft of the provincial water forces.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Qianlong's generals (Zhaohui, Fude) destroyed the Dzungars and took the Tarim basin 1755-59 with supply lines across the Gansu corridor (Perdue, China Marches West, 2005, not consulted directly).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: banner corps identity strong but discipline in decline (Elliott); Green Standard dispersed in small detachments.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: fresh from the Dzungar and Altishahr victories.

weapons.note: Anchor 5 (1600): matchlocks and cast cannon; European armies were already near anchor 6 (flintlock, bayonet).

armor.note: Anchor 4-5: brigandine and padded armour, mostly parade wear by 1760.

ships.note: Anchor 4-5: war junks, not ships of the line.

fortification.note: Anchor 5 minus: massive brick city walls and the Great Wall, no bastioned trace.

logistics.note: Anchor 5-6: state granaries, the Grand Canal and Perdue's grain-transport system across Gansu sustained armies 2,000 km from China proper.

communications.note: Anchor 5: yizhan relay courier system with palace memorial channels.

isr.note: Anchor 5 minus: post-station reporting and Mongol scouts; Jesuit-surveyed maps.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 China 1760 = 1,022 (2011 int$); range is the usual uncertainty of the series.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Military pay was the largest item of a small central budget (land tax frozen in 1713); low = peacetime, high = Dzungar campaign years.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Cotton and silk textiles, porcelain, salt, iron.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Ever-normal granaries stocked tens of millions of shi; New World crops raised output.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Imperial post roads linking ~1,900 relay stations; Gansu corridor road extended to Ili.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo, Shanghai, Tianjin, Zhapu, Dengzhou.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Large coastal and Nanyang junk trade; no aggregate tonnage figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. State grain convoys, military farms and purchased Kazakh horses carried campaigns deep into Dzungaria (Perdue).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules, camels, oxen and water buffalo across the empire and Mongolia.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: walled cities, population support in China proper, deep strategic depth.

notes: Snapshot = 1760, Qianlong after the conquest of Dzungaria and Altishahr (1755-59) and before the Burma war (1765-69). Personnel convention: the salaried Eight Banners (>200,000) and Green Standard Army (600,067) are activePersonnel; Mongol jasagh levies, tusi native troops and banner supernumeraries are trainedReserves. The split of the 800,000 into roles is an educated reading of the banner/Green Standard structure (Elliott, The Manchu Way, 2001; Waley-Cohen, The Culture of War in China, 2006), neither consulted directly. Border: nearest file containing the polity is world_1715; it lacks Xinjiang. Population convention: China proper, Manchuria, Mongolia, Tibet and Xinjiang; vassals (Korea, Vietnam, Burma later) excluded.
